title: The cost of direction in quantum Bell certification
summary: Certifying a quantum bound can require more information than realizing the correlations that attain it. We show that this distinction becomes unbounded when a proof must condition on one party's measurement question. A fixed Bell scenario attained by one entangled qubit pair has a standard degree-two sum-of-squares certificate, yet the minimum degree in either conditioning direction grows as the inverse square root of the distance to a local endpoint.
